name: KY-017 tilt switch
identification: Small black PCB with 3 angled header pins at one end and a black cylinder lying flat along the board. The KY-002 has a similar cylinder standing upright.

middle.say: middle pin, the one between S and minus

confirmations.question: Look at the 3 pins of the tilt switch. Is one marked S and one marked with a minus, with the third pin between them?
confirmations.reason: The pin order differs between modules. The wiring plan is only valid if S and minus are the outer pins and the supply pin is the one in the middle.

facts.statement: The module has three pins: signal (printed S), supply (+V, the middle pin) and ground (printed -). The vendor's drawing shows them in the order -, supply, S. Go by the printed markings.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-017, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor wires the module to 3.3 V on Raspberry Pi, Pico or micro:bit and to 5 V on a classic Arduino. No supply rating is published.
A ball inside closes a contact depending on the tilt. The vendor's example reports a tilt while the signal is LOW. Powered from 3.3 V the signal cannot rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-017, description and code example
